questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

It's so stressful to think that what you have build with hard work is at risk.

options.text: think that what you have build
with hard work is at risk.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect form of the verb "**build**".
 
• The correct past participle form of "build" is "**built**."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**think that what you have built**," ensuring grammatical correctness.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It's so stressful to think that what you have **built **__with hard work is at risk."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 1.
 
• **Option 3: It's so stressful to** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: with hard work is at risk.** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Select the sentence with an error in the adverb used.

options.text: They performed the task surprisingly well despite the challenges.
She had scarcely begun her speech when the microphone failed.
He spoke softly enough to avoid waking the baby.
The solution was applied so effective that it resolved the issue immediately.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. The solution was applied so effective that it resolved the issue immediately .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the given sentence is the use of the adverb "**effective**." The correct adverb should be "**effectively**."
 
• "**Effective**" is an adjective, whereas "effectively" is the adverb form that modifies the verb "was applied" correctly.
 
• To correct the sentence, replace "effective" with "effectively": "The solution was applied so effectively that it resolved the issue immediately."

Correct sentence: *The solution was applied so **effectively** that it resolved the issue immediately.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **They performed the task surprisingly well despite the challenges:** Correct usage. "Surprisingly" modifies the adverb "well."
 
• **She had scarcely begun her speech when the microphone failed:** Correct usage. "Scarcely" modifies the verb "begun."
 
• **He spoke softly enough to avoid waking the baby:** Correct usage. "Softly" modifies the verb "spoke."

questions.solution:

__
 
• The error lies in the part ' in recent time.'
 
• According to the rules of nouns **'time'** is an uncountable noun and it is singular in form.
 
• Here in the given sentence, the mishap of pollution caused due to burning of fossil fuel but, we don't know the definite number of time.
 
• Therefore we have to use the plural of 'time' which is **'times.'**
 
• In the given sentence we need to use 'in recent times' in place of 'in recent time' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 

Correct sentence:__ *The burning** of fossil fuels is causing pollution **in recent times.***

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

__Has__ Gita __any__ previous knowledge of __work with__ junior colleagues?
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 4) i.e. 'work.'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'work.'
 
• We can note that the preposition **'of'** is used before the word **'work,' **which is a verb.
 
• The word that must come after 'of' should be the **object** of the preposition 'of'. Hence, a **gerund** (working) must be placed after it.
 
• A **gerund** is a verb that ends in** '-ing'** and functions as a noun or object.
 
• Therefore we need to use the gerund form of the verb 'work' which is **'working'** after the preposition 'of.'
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'working' in place of 'work' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__* Has Gita any previous knowledge of **working** with junior colleagues?*

• The use of the word 'protest' in the sentence indicates **an action that shows that you do not like or approve of something**.

• The preposition 'in' is used **for showing the activity somebody is involved in**.
